note: Every wording change made to haunt regulars' voice notes when softening forced catchphrases (2026-09-30, Ingram's /goal). Applied by tools/art-review/apply-edits.mjs; each is an exact-substring replacement inside one canon scene file, and every application is recorded in ledger.json for the review page. Nothing outside these strings is touched.

edits.find: Calls them 'passengers', which is not a compliment, and makes them wait while the dockworkers go in first.
edits.replace: Lets the dockworkers go in ahead of them and leaves them standing on the step, which says everything she means to say.
edits.why: A nickname used as an insult, replaced by an action that carries the same meaning.

edits.find: Calls them 'sailor', saves them the stools nearest the hot tap, and tells them who on the island is worth knowing.
edits.replace: Saves them the stools nearest the hot tap, and tells them who on the island is worth knowing.
edits.why: The forced pet name 'sailor' is dropped; the warmth is already in what she does for them.

edits.find: Blows the brass whistle before she says anything important.
edits.replace: The brass whistle hangs at her collar, and the room goes quiet a beat before she lifts it.
edits.why: Same habit, shown as an effect on the room rather than a rule.

edits.find: Calls the pools 'forward' and 'aft', the lockers 'the locker deck', and everyone 'sailor' once she likes them.
edits.replace: The bathhouse runs on bells and a logbook: lockers numbered like cabins, and the water's temperature chalked up every hour like a ship's heading.
edits.why: The ship-running-a-bathhouse idea is now told through her routines, not a vocabulary she recites.

edits.find: "Soap on the stool, sailor, not on the tiles. I've seen a stevedore go down like a felled tree."
edits.replace: "Soap on the stool, not on the tiles. I once watched a stevedore go down like a felled tree."
edits.why: Removes 'sailor'.

edits.find: Wash before you get in, and the towel never touches the water. Welcome aboard.
edits.replace: Wash before you get in, and the towel never touches the water.
edits.why: 'Welcome aboard' was the ship gag shouted in her first line; the rules already do the work.

edits.find: and calls them 'my young ones' to anyone who'll listen.
edits.replace: and talks about them to anyone who'll listen as if he had trained them himself.
edits.why: Same warmth, no stock phrase.

edits.find: Calls every Frame 'she' and every pilot 'that boy' or 'that girl', however old they were.
edits.replace: Talks about Frames the way people talk about old horses, and about pilots the way people talk about somebody else's children.
edits.why: Gives the same information as a way of speaking, not a naming rule.

edits.find: Calls everything that isn't boiling 'lukewarm'.
edits.replace: Sinks into the hottest pool without a flinch and looks mildly let down by the temperature.
edits.why: 'Lukewarm' as a catchphrase became a visible behaviour.

edits.find: "This? Lukewarm. At home we would put the babies in this."
edits.replace: "This one? At home we bathe the babies in this."
edits.why: Keeps the joke, drops the word.

edits.find: Says 'the board says' when she means 'I say'.
edits.replace: Lets the board do her talking: a rule is a rule because it is up there, in her handwriting.
edits.why: The habit is the same but no longer a formula.

edits.find: "The board says the sinks, so it's the sinks."
edits.replace: "It's the sinks. I've already written it down."
edits.why: Removes 'the board says'.

edits.find: Calls everyone 'friend' from the moment he meets them.
edits.replace: Gets more generous the closer he is to cheating: the drinks are on him, the good seat is yours.
edits.why: 'Friend' as a tic replaced by a tell the table can learn to spot.

edits.find: New blood! Sit by me, friend. I'll explain the rules
edits.replace: New blood! Sit by me. I'll explain the rules
edits.why: Removes 'friend'.

edits.find: "Friend, I'd never cheat you. I'd cheat Michiru, but never you."
edits.replace: "I'd never cheat you. Michiru, now, that's a matter of principle."
edits.why: Removes 'friend'.

edits.find: Says "Lights, please" instead of "lights out", as if she were asking.
edits.replace: Asks for lights out rather than ordering it, and thanks the room when it complies.
edits.why: The politeness stays; the stock phrase goes.

edits.find: Says "at home" at the start of half his sentences.
edits.replace: Brings up home the way people press a bruise, mostly by accident, and then looks embarrassed.
edits.why: Homesickness shown instead of a repeated phrase.

edits.find: "At home we'd have been asleep for three hours by now."
edits.replace: "By now I'd have been asleep three hours, with the river going."
edits.why: Keeps the image, drops 'At home'.

edits.find: Calls every broken thing "a patient".
edits.replace: Handles broken things like patients: gently, and talking to them quietly.
edits.why: The catchphrase 'a patient' is now a way of behaving.

edits.find: "Hand me that. No, the other patient."
edits.replace: "Hand me that. No, the one with the limp."
edits.why: Same joke without the word.

edits.find: Calls the hour like a ship's bell: "Two o'clock, and all's damp."
edits.replace: Knocks the hour out on the brass rail with one knuckle, one knock for each hour, and only afterwards says the number.
edits.why: A shouted formula turned into a habit of action.

edits.find: Calls everyone by their job: "Pit", "Bench", "Crane".
edits.replace: Directs the shop by station rather than by name, so everyone hears their own job called back at them.
edits.why: Same trait described rather than quoted.

edits.find: Gives everyone on the floor a nickname from the top of their head: "Red Hat", "Tall One".
edits.replace: Names people from twenty metres up by whatever she can see of them: a hat, a height, a limp.
edits.why: Nicknames described as how she sees people from the cab.

edits.find: Says who told her everything, with a rating out of five.
edits.replace: Never repeats a rumour without saying who she got it from and how far she trusts them.
edits.why: The 'out of five' gag removed; her care over sources remains.

edits.find: "That's from a laundry girl, so four out of five."
edits.replace: "That's from a laundry girl, and laundry girls are never wrong about a hem."
edits.why: Removes the rating formula.

edits.find: Says 'in fact' before things that are not facts.
edits.replace: Is at his most certain a moment before he turns out to be wrong.
edits.why: The joke 'in fact' becomes a pattern the table can enjoy spotting.

edits.find: "In fact, the cellar is just potatoes. I checked twice."
edits.replace: "The cellar is just potatoes. I checked twice, and I was very thorough."
edits.why: Removes 'In fact'.

edits.find: Calls everyone 'dear'.
edits.replace: Is so gentle with everyone that it takes a while to notice she is counting them.
edits.why: 'Dear' was also Tsubaki's word and Imai's; hers is now a manner.

edits.find: "Lamp out, dear. I'm counting to ten, very slowly."
edits.replace: "Lamp out. I'm counting to ten, very slowly."
edits.why: Removes 'dear'.

edits.find: Says 'connecting you' when she introduces people to each other.
edits.replace: Introduces people by patching them together: a hand on each elbow, a small pause, and then they are talking.
edits.why: The exchange operator's phrase turned into the gesture behind it.

edits.find: "Tokuji, these are candidates. Candidates, Tokuji. Connecting you."
edits.replace: "Tokuji, these are candidates. Candidates, Tokuji. There."
edits.why: Removes 'Connecting you'.

edits.find: Calls every star 'she'.
edits.replace: Talks about stars the way other people talk about relatives: strong opinions, no doubt at all.
edits.why: Same personification, less of a rule.

edits.find: "No, left of that. Left. Your other left. There she is."
edits.replace: "No, left of that. Left. Further. There."
edits.why: 'Your other left' also appeared in Mrs Handa's lines; it now belongs only to her.

edits.find: Calls every candidate 'young sir' or 'young miss', whatever they are.
edits.replace: Addresses every candidate as if they were a visiting officer, however young.
edits.why: Stock forms of address replaced by his manner.

edits.find: Calls everyone by their crew, or 'candidate' if they have none.
edits.replace: Knows everyone by crew before she knows their name; anyone without one is simply a candidate until proven otherwise.
edits.why: Reads as her character instead of a label.

edits.find: Starts every story 'So.'
edits.replace: Takes a breath like a man about to dive before every story, and the room leans in.
edits.why: The opening word 'So.' becomes a physical habit.

edits.find: "So. There I am, halfway up a leg, and the leg starts walking."
edits.replace: "There I am, halfway up a leg, and the leg starts walking."
edits.why: Removes 'So.'.

edits.find: Calls them 'my candidates' and fights anyone who says a word against them.
edits.replace: Introduces them to strangers as his own candidates and fights anyone who says a word against them.
edits.why: Same loyalty, told as an action.

edits.find: Says 'properly' a lot.
edits.replace: Picks his words carefully, as if he might be marked on them.
edits.why: 'Properly' as a tic becomes his anxiety to sound older.

edits.find: "Did you see one move? Properly move?"
edits.replace: "Did you see one move? Actually move?"
edits.why: Removes 'properly'.

edits.find: "I'm on Crew Three. I'm properly on it now."
edits.replace: "I'm on Crew Three. It's official. I've seen the sheet."
edits.why: Removes 'properly'.

edits.find: Calls the ward 'the ship', the nurse 'the captain', and the patients 'passengers'.
edits.replace: Describes the ward as if it were a ship in a bad harbour, and treats the night sister as its captain.
edits.why: The renamed-everything gag becomes a way of seeing.

edits.find: Ah, new passengers. Welcome aboard. The captain is at the far end, and she runs a very tight ship.
edits.replace: Ah, new arrivals. The night sister is at the far end, and she runs a very tight ship.
edits.why: Keeps one nautical wink; drops the stack of ship words.

edits.find: and calls them 'my crew'.
edits.replace: and starts treating them as his crew.
edits.why: Same warmth, told as behaviour.

edits.find: Says 'Putting you through' when she changes the subject.
edits.replace: Changes the subject the way an operator changes a line: no warning, a small click, and you are somewhere else.
edits.why: The catchphrase you asked me to drop from her file was still in the scene; the habit stays, the phrase goes.

edits.find: "Hold the line, dear, I'm getting to it."
edits.replace: "Hold on, dear, I'm getting to it."
edits.why: Drops the switchboard stock phrase.

edits.find: Calls a whole table 'you two', whatever the actual number.
edits.replace: Counts a table by heads before she pours, and has never once got a tab wrong.
edits.why: A verbal quirk replaced by a competence you can see.

edits.find: "You two are drinking slower than you're talking. Fix one of those."
edits.replace: "You're drinking slower than you're talking. Fix one of those."
edits.why: Removes 'you two'.

edits.find: Calls every audience 'my dears', and every town by its name, as if it were a person.
edits.replace: Greets a town by name like an old friend she is slightly worried about.
edits.why: 'My dears' dropped; the town-as-a-person idea kept.

edits.find: and when she has to, calls them 'the ones who know better'.
edits.replace: and when she has to speak of them, refers to them as the people who know better.
edits.why: Reads as a description rather than a quoted label.

edits.find: Says 'right' before he does anything.
edits.replace: Puts a hand on something solid before he starts any job, as if the floor might argue.
edits.why: The verbal tic became a physical habit.

edits.find: "Right. Mind the cable."
edits.replace: "Mind the cable."
edits.why: Removes 'Right.'

edits.find: Says 'now then' before she tells anyone off.
edits.replace: Draws herself up an inch before she tells anyone off, so you always get a moment to reconsider.
edits.why: The catchphrase became a warning sign.

edits.find: "Now then. Feet off the bench."
edits.replace: "Feet off the bench."
edits.why: Removes 'Now then.'
